review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/evidence.go:44 — effectiveStatus diverges from FinalizeStage.Run. effectiveStatus requires allDone (every task.Status == "done") AND all three gates to return ready_for_review, but FinalizeStage was simplified in this diff to check only the three gates. A run with a failed task from an earlier cycle but all gates passing will be finalized as ready_for_review by FinalizeStage yet show needs_human in every evidence file written by EvidenceStage. (suggested fix: Remove the allDone loop from effectiveStatus and mirror FinalizeStage's logic: return ready_for_review when FinalValidationPassed && FinalReviewPassed && FinalAcceptancePassed, regardless of individual task statuses.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/plan.go:14 — maxTaskID in plan.go duplicates maxTaskIDInQueue in taskloop.go. Both parse t-NNN suffixes; any format change must be made in two places. (suggested fix: Extract a shared parseTaskIDNum helper into the specloop package and call it from both sites.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/taskloop.go:122 — The baseline capture call to DetectFilesChanged silently discards its error with //nolint:errcheck. If the call fails the baseline is never captured; the second (delta) call will also treat itself as a baseline capture (since baseline remains nil), silently returning empty and missing all file changes for that task. (suggested fix: Return the error from the baseline call or, if baseline capture fails, mark the detector as disabled for this task iteration and fall back to runner-reported FilesChanged.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/files_changed.go:55 — hashAllFiles always returns a nil error — every error path inside the function handles the failure locally and continues. The caller's `if err != nil` branch is dead code, and the error return type on the function signature is misleading. (suggested fix: Change the signature to `func hashAllFiles(absDir string) map[string]string` and remove the dead error check at the call site.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/evidence.go:44 — `effectiveStatus` checks both task statuses (allDone loop) AND the three gate booleans to determine ready_for_review, but `FinalizeStage.Run` was simplified in this diff to check only the three gates (removing the allDone requirement). A run with failed tasks from earlier cycles that passes all three gates will be finalized as ready_for_review by FinalizeStage, but effectiveStatus will return needs_human — causing review.md and summary.md to disagree with the actual final status. (suggested fix: Remove the allDone check from effectiveStatus to match FinalizeStage's gate-only logic: `if rs.FinalValidationPassed && rs.FinalReviewPassed && rs.FinalAcceptancePassed { return ready_for_review }`.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/taskloop.go:122 — Error from the DetectFilesChanged baseline call is silently suppressed with `//nolint:errcheck`. If the baseline capture fails, the subsequent delta call will compare against a nil map, potentially reporting spurious file changes or missing real ones. (suggested fix: Log or propagate the baseline error rather than silencing it; at minimum fall back to the runner's own FilesChanged on baseline failure.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/plan.go:15 — `maxTaskID(tasks []runstore.Task)` in plan.go and `maxTaskIDInQueue(queue []taskEntry)` in taskloop.go implement identical t-NNN parsing logic.
